# Rights, Duties and Directive Principles

<!-- STEP id="rights-card" -->
## Fundamental Rights

The Constitution sets out three different things. **Fundamental Rights** are claims that citizens can make, and a court can enforce them.

<!-- STEP id="duties-card" -->
## Fundamental Duties

**Fundamental Duties** are what the Constitution asks of citizens, such as respecting the Constitution and protecting public property.

<!-- STEP id="principles-card" -->
## Directive Principles

**Directive Principles of State Policy** guide the State when it makes policy, but a court does not enforce them. Article 46 is one, and you will meet it in Lesson 4.

**Rights belong to citizens, duties are asked of citizens, and Directive Principles guide the State.**
